title: Sycophancy Spotter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Classification activity in which learners decide whether the model reply in each of six illustrative researcher-model exchanges is sycophantic or calibrated. Six exchanges in a fixed order, one attempt each; the correct classification is always revealed with a one-sentence reason, and the run ends with a score out of 6 and a mastery statement at 5 of 6.

educational.topic: Recognizing sycophantic and calibrated model replies
learningObjectives: Distinguish, among six exchanges between a researcher and a model, the replies that are sycophantic from those that are calibrated, with at least 5 of 6 classified correctly
prerequisites: Sycophancy, overconfidence, uncertainty awareness, and the countermeasures, as defined in the section Behaviors of Models That Undermine Checks of Chapter 17

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons reachable with the Tab key; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and the symbols check mark and X as well as a color-blind-safe blue and orange pair; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Sycophantic
controls.purpose: Submits the classification sycophantic for the current exchange. Disabled after the answer is submitted.

controls.label: Calibrated
controls.purpose: Submits the classification calibrated for the current exchange. Disabled after the answer is submitted.

controls.label: Next Exchange / See Score / Start Over
controls.purpose: Enabled after an answer is submitted. Advances to the next exchange, shows the score after exchange 6, and on the summary screen starts a new run of the same six exchanges.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Binary classification with one attempt per item and immediate explanatory feedback
keyQuestions: Did the reply follow the evidence or the researcher?
Was new evidence supplied before the model changed its answer?
Does the reply state what it cannot establish and what would establish it?
commonMisconceptions: A model that changes its answer is being responsive
A polite and agreeable reply is a good reply
A model that declines to confirm is being unhelpful
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score of at least 5 of 6 classifications matching the answer key is evidence of mastery
Reading the definitions is exploration and is not evidence
Learner explains why exchanges 2 and 3 receive different classifications
